 Comment React Share Flavio Cobolli Retires in Tears in Vienna: Berrettini Confirms Injury
 Trailing 5-2 to Matteo Berrettini, Flavio Cobolli left the court in tears. His compatriot confirmed that an injury forced the retirement, just weeks before the ATP Finals.
 Italy's Flavio Cobolli looks on during his match against Canada's Felix Auger-Aliassime in the men's singles quarterfinals on day 11 of the Roland-Garros tennis tournament on Court Philippe-Chatrier at the Roland-Garros complex in Paris, June 3, 2026. © ALAIN JOCARD / AFP Jules Hypolite 29/10/2026, 20:44 1 min to read Follow us ATP 500 Berrettini Cobolli Vienne An unexpected scene brought the day to a close in Vienna.
 Trailing 5-2 to his compatriot Matteo Berrettini in the second round, Flavio Cobolli retired after being seen in tears on his bench.
 Remove ads Cobolli leaves the court in tears
 The start of the match was evenly balanced, before Berrettini took the lead at 3-2 thanks to a break converted on his fifth opportunity of the set.
 The former world No. 6 then consolidated his advantage, until Cobolli decided to throw in the towel, visibly deeply affected. Berrettini immediately went over to comfort him.
 In his post-match interview, Matteo Berrettini confirmed that the Roland-Garros finalist had retired due to an injury:
 "I feel sorry for him. I've been through this kind of situation many times myself. I know he wants to play in Turin. The worst thing that can happen is getting injured just a few weeks before such an event."
 Is his ATP Finals qualification in danger?
 Currently 6th in the Race, Flavio Cobolli is still in contention for a spot at the ATP Finals in Turin.
 This injury, the nature of which is still unknown, could however complicate his chances of competing in the Masters for the first time in his career.
 Berrettini, meanwhile, advances to the quarterfinals in Vienna, where he will face Alex de Minaur.
